corpus.text: kube-llmops is a Kubernetes-native LLMOps platform that uses Umbrella Helm Charts. It was created in 2024 and provides 15 sub-charts deployed via a single helm install command. The platform runs on k3s clusters with NVIDIA GPU support and supports vLLM, llama.cpp, and TEI as model serving engines.

LiteLLM serves as the AI Gateway in kube-llmops, running on port 4000. It provides a unified OpenAI-compatible API that routes requests to different backend engines (vLLM, llama.cpp, TEI). LiteLLM supports rate limiting, budget management, and integrates with Langfuse for tracing. The master key for authentication is configured via the masterKey Helm value.

Langfuse v3 is used for LLM observability and tracing in kube-llmops. It requires ClickHouse for OLAP trace storage, Redis for async worker queues, and S3-compatible storage (MinIO) for event and media blob uploads. Every LiteLLM request is automatically traced via the success_callback and failure_callback configuration.

vLLM is the primary model serving engine in kube-llmops. It uses PagedAttention for efficient GPU memory management. The default GPU memory utilization is set to 0.8 (80%). vLLM serves models via an OpenAI-compatible API on port 8000. The enforce-eager flag is used for Blackwell GPU compatibility.

TEI (Text Embeddings Inference) by HuggingFace provides embedding and reranking services. The default embedding model is BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 which produces 384-dimensional vectors. TEI runs on port 8080 and supports both the native /embed endpoint and the OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint.

pgvector is the vector storage backend in kube-llmops, running as an extension in PostgreSQL 16. The pgvector/pgvector:pg16 Docker image is used, and the vector extension is automatically enabled via the PostgreSQL init script. Dify uses pgvector for storing document embeddings for RAG retrieval.

Dify is the RAG application platform in kube-llmops version 1.13.2. It consists of 5 components: API server, Web frontend, Worker (Celery), Plugin Daemon, and Redis. The Plugin Daemon manages model provider plugins and requires its own database (dify_plugin). Dify uses a single-domain path-based routing with Ingress.

MinIO provides S3-compatible object storage in kube-llmops. It is used by both Langfuse (for event/media storage) and Dify (for file storage). The default credentials are minioadmin/minioadmin. Buckets are auto-created on startup via mkdir in the MinIO entrypoint.

Keycloak v26.5.6 provides SSO authentication for kube-llmops. It uses an embedded H2 database for development mode and supports OIDC protocol. Realm configuration is imported from a ConfigMap on startup. Grafana SSO uses internalIssuerUrl for server-side token exchange with the cluster-internal Keycloak address.

The monitoring stack in kube-llmops includes Prometheus v3.9.1 for metrics collection, Grafana v12.4.1 for dashboards, DCGM Exporter for GPU metrics, and the OpenTelemetry Collector for trace aggregation. Loki and Fluent Bit handle log collection and forwarding.

The Helm umbrella chart pattern allows deploying all kube-llmops components with a single command: helm install kube-llmops charts/kube-llmops-stack -f values-single-node.yaml. This deploys vLLM, LiteLLM, Langfuse, TEI, Dify, PostgreSQL, MinIO, Prometheus, Grafana, and Keycloak.

The Ragas evaluation framework is used in kube-llmops to measure RAG quality. It computes four key metrics: Faithfulness (is the answer grounded in context), Answer Relevancy (is the answer relevant to the question), Context Precision (is the retrieved context relevant), and Context Recall (does the context cover the ground truth).

The LiteLLM configuration uses huggingface/ prefix for embedding models with drop_params: true to handle incompatible parameters like encoding_format. For LLM models, it uses openai/ prefix to route to vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API.

Dify's Plugin Daemon manages model provider plugins. It requires its own PostgreSQL database (dify_plugin), Redis for caching, and persistent storage for plugin working directories. The OpenAI-API-compatible plugin enables Dify to use any OpenAI-compatible backend like LiteLLM.

The automated Dify setup Job performs five steps: wait for API readiness, create admin account, login with session cookies, install plugins from pre-bundled .difypkg files, and configure LLM and embedding model providers. It runs as a Helm post-install/post-upgrade hook.
